location: South Fork, Colorado — Northwest Coast Masks, Museum of Mankind
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. N.F. Wechel, 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, Kansas 67208
notes: Souvenir card from the British Museum's Museum of Mankind (© 1976), showing a carved wooden Northwest Coast headdress mask with a raven's beak and five small animal heads, 27cm tall. 9¢ "Right of People Peaceably to Assemble" stamp. Message: "Arr. yesterday P.M. and everything just same as a year ago. Ate out with Bill last nite & today we've been getting acquainted again with the area. Tomorrow nite will attend a big community elk & deer barbeque. The weather is ideal & the Mts. beautiful. Birds found my feeders this evening. Hope it rains & cools off again there. Geo. & Alice."
front: 1977 - Museum of Mankind, Great Britain - front.jpeg
back: 1977 - Museum of Mankind, Great Britain - back.jpeg
feed_description: Geo. & Alice settle back into their South Fork, Colorado cabin for the summer of 1977 — feeders full of birds, an elk-and-deer barbeque on the calendar — sent on a British Museum mask souvenir card.

location: Government Camp, Oregon — Timberline Lodge, Mount Hood
recipient: Mrs. Stella Obszany (surname best-guess from cursive), 322 Nash Rd., New Bedford, Massachusetts 02746
notes: Aerial photo of Timberline Lodge on Mount Hood's south slope, "North America's only year-round ski resort" (photo: Jim Vincent, publ. Smith-Western Inc., Portland). 10¢ "We hold these Truths" Jefferson stamp. Message: "1-3-81. Hi, It's great up here, so high I feel dizzy. You'll love the view when you come, about 1 hr. 15 min. from our house. Love, Jan."
feed_description: Jan writes home from a snowy, high-altitude visit to Timberline Lodge in January 1981, promising Stella in New Bedford, Mass. a view worth the trip.

location: Offenbach am Main, Hesse, Germany — Blick in die Bieberer Straße
year: c. mid-1950s (20pf Heuss Bundespost stamps, issued 1954–1960; postmark date not fully legible)
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. R. McKinnon, 940 McPherson St., St. Louis, Missouri
notes: Black-and-white street view of Offenbach am Main's Bieberer Straße, showing the Städtische Sparkasse building. Sent air mail ("Mit Luftpost / Par Avion" label). Return address partly legible: Schöning & Co., Lübeck, possibly with a Berlin branch line (faint, best guess). Message: "Dear Dottie & Bob (recipient's first name a best guess from 'R. McKinnon'), Home again and it's just as nice as ever. I'm taking care of my mother, she's very ill. With God's help I'll have her come to the States as soon as possible. I'll be back in Boston in October, please write! Take care of yourselves. Love, Inge."
feed_description: Inge writes home to St. Louis from Offenbach am Main, back in Germany to care for her ailing mother and hoping to bring her to the States — a quieter, harder note than most in the archive.
